content.thinking:
Let me analyze this OIML certificate for a water meter.

Key facts:
- Certificate number: R49/2013-A-SK1-2023.06
- Scheme: A
- Member State: Slovakia (SLOVAKIA)
- Issuing Authority: Slovak Legal Metrology (SLM), Hviedzoslavova 1124/31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia
- Person responsible: Dušan Šmigura, Director of PCB
- Applicant: Zhejiang Diyuan Instrument Co., Ltd., No. 106, Chunhan Road, Beiyuan Subdistrict, Yiwu, Zhejiang, P.R. China
- Manufacturer: same as applicant
- Certified type: Water meter YYD-S
- Module: Electromagnetic water meters with electronic indication device
- Recommendation: OIML R 49, Edition 2013 (year 2013), accuracy class 2
- Page total: 8
- Date issued: 13 December 2023 (from revision history "Certificate first issued" and signature date)

Project number? There's no explicit project number. OIML issuer ID? Not explicit. Hmm, the certificate number includes "SK1". Not clearly an oiml_issuer_id field. I'll omit if not present. Actually "V03-23-01-10" is a form code. FK-P05-85 is form code. Not oiml_issuer_id.

Test reports:
1. OIML Test report No: 2023/CV006/312.15 dated 8th December 2023, 50 pages, role: test_report
2. OIML Type Evaluation Report No. 2023/ER006/SK1 dated 8th December 2023, 16 pages, role: type_evaluation_report
3. Technical documentation file "Technical documentation file Zhejiang Diyuan_YYD-S_00" dated 8th December 2023, 58 pages, role: documentation_file

Revision history:
- Revision "0", 13th December 2023, "Certificate first issued"

Technical and metrological data — this is a matrix by DN (nominal diameter) and R ratio:

Water meter type YYD-S
- Accuracy class: 2
- DN: 40, 50 (mm)
- Q3: 25 (DN40), 40 (DN50) m³/h
- Q1: for DN40: 0.250, 0.156, 0.100; for DN50: 0.400, 0.250, 0.160 (m³/h)
- Q2: for DN40: 0.400, 0.250, 0.160; for DN50: 0.640, 0.400, 0.256 (m³/h)
- Q4: DN40: 31.3; DN50: 50 (m³/h)
- Q3/Q1 ratio: R = 100, 160, 250 for DN40; 100, 160, 250 for DN50
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- Connection thread: Flange
- Construction length L: 200 mm
- Installation orientation: H (horizontal)
- Water temperature range: 0.1 to 50 °C, temperature class T50
- MAP: 16 bar
- Pressure loss: 0.40 bar, class Δp 40
- MPE upper: ±2% (at temp ≤30°C), ±3% (at >30°C)
- MPE lower: ±5%
- Capacity of calculator: 99999.9999 m³
- Scale interval: 0.0001 m³
- Mechanical class: M1
- Climatic class: -40 to +70 °C
- Electromagnetic class: E2
- Environmental classification: O
- Flow profile sensitivity class: U5/D3
- Protection class: IP68
- Battery: replaceable li-battery 3.6 V, life 6 years

So the model family: 6 variants (2 DN × 3 R ratios):
- DN40 R100: Q1=0.250, Q2=0.400, Q3=25, Q4=31.3
- DN40 R160: Q1=0.156, Q2=0.250
- DN40 R250: Q1=0.100, Q2=0.160
- DN50 R100: Q1=0.400, Q2=0.640, Q3=40, Q4=50
- DN50 R160: Q1=0.250, Q2=0.400
- DN50 R250: Q1=0.160, Q2=0.256

Wait — check Q4 for DN50: 50 m³/h. Q4 = 1.25 × Q3 = 50. Yes. Q4 DN40 = 31.3? 1.25 × 25 = 31.25 ≈ 31.3. Yes.

Model IDs: I'll use "DN40-R100", "DN40-R160", "DN40-R250", "DN50-R100", "DN50-R160", "DN50-R250".

Model-level characteristics:
- nominal_diameter: DN40: 40, DN50: 50, unit mm
- permanent_flowrate_q3: DN40: 25, DN50: 40, unit m³/h
- minimum_flowrate_q1: each of 6, unit m³/h
- transitional_flowrate_q2: each of 6, unit m³/h
- overload_flowrate_q4: DN40: 31.3, DN50: 50, unit m³/h
- ratio_q3_q1: 100, 160, 250 per variant, unit R (dimensionless)

Type-level characteristics:
- accuracy_class: 2
- ratio_q2_q1: 1.6
- connection_thread: "Flange" (string value)
- construction_length: 200 mm
- installation_orientation: "H"
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, unit °C
- temperature_class: "T50"
- maximum_admissible_pressure_map: 16 bar
- pressure_loss: 0.40 bar
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 40" — hmm, canonical label without LaTeX. "pressure_loss_class" value "Δp 40"? Value could be "Δp40" or just 40 with class. I'll use value "Δp 40" — but rule says no trailing punctuation; Δp is not LaTeX. Actually maybe simpler: pressure_loss_class: {value: "Δp 40"}. Hmm, the canonical label can't have LaTeX. "Δp" is fine as a Unicode character. Let me keep value "Δp 40".
- maximum_permitted_error_upper_flowrates: {min: -2, max: 2}? Or ±2 — better as string "±2"? The rules say numbers not strings but ±2 has sign range. I could record as {min: -2, max: 2} with unit %. And condition "at water temperature ≤ 30°C" and ±3 at >30°C. Maybe use config_level for MPE by temperature. Actually the MPE is a function of temperature: ±2 (≤30°C), ±3 (>30°C). This is a config axis: water temperature. Let me use config_level:
  - attribute: maximum_permitted_error_upper_range, axis: water_temperature, values: [{condition: "≤30 °C", value: -2..2}, {condition: ">30 °C", value: -3..3}]
  
  Hmm, but ± as a value: {min: -2, max: 2} makes sense. Or keep string "±2". I'll use {min:-2,max:2} — wait but ±5 for lower: {min:-5, max:5}.

  Alternatively simpler: value "±2" as string. The rule says "Numbers, not strings" for numeric values. ±2 is effectively numeric with sign range. I'll use min/max objects: {min: -2, max: 2}. Hmm, but that might be misinterpreted as a range. Alternatively record MPE as positive tolerance with a note. Let me record value as string "±2" for clarity? The strict rule: "Numbers, not strings. `3000` not `"3000"`." For ±, I think using {min, max} is a reasonable representation. Actually MPE is a tolerance — value ±2% means error in [-2%, +2%]. {min:-2, max:2} captures that. I'll go with that.

- maximum_permitted_error_lower_flowrates: {min:-5, max:5}, unit %
- capacity_of_calculator: 99999.9999 m³
- scale_interval: 0.0001 m³
- mechanical_class: "M1"
- climatic_class: {min:-40, max:70}, unit °C
- electromagnetic_class: "E2"
- environmental_classification: "O"
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U5/D3"
- protection_class: "IP68" (note "Protektion class" typo — use protection_class)
- battery: replaceable li-battery, 3.6 V, life 6 years. Record as characteristics: battery_voltage 3.6 V, battery_life 6 years? Also from description: 4 pcs lithium batteries 3.6 V 76 Ah for flow rate and 2 pcs 3.6 V 38 Ah for data collector. Battery life 6 years.

Config_level: MPE vs temperature axis.

Matrix table: dimensions table (Fig 2):
- Diameter 40: rated pressure 1.6 MPa, L 200, H 333, D 150, weight 13 kg
- Diameter 50: rated pressure 1.6 MPa, L 200, H 342, D 165, weight 14 kg

I'll include this in matrix_tables as "dimensions" table.

Software: version 2.14u, checksum 14230. Include as type_level characteristic? Or matrix_tables? Could include software_version: "2.14u", software_checksum: "14230". I'll add to type_level.

Components: Flow sensor (electromagnetic transducer), Calculator and indication device (converter). Include as components:
- role: "flow_sensor", type_designations: [] (no designation), description... schema doesn't have description for components, but has characteristics{}. I can put characteristics like measurement principle. Actually schema: components[]: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. I'll add brief characteristics.
- role: "calculator_and_indication_device"

Also non-essential parts: communication RS485, antenna.

Footnotes: none present.

Characteristics with footnotes: none.

Certificate-level:
- number: "R49/2013-A-SK1-2023.06"
- scheme: "A"
- project_number: not present — omit. Hmm, maybe "2023.06"? Not clearly a project number. The test report numbers contain 2023/CV006 and 2023/ER006 — "006" could be project. But not stated. Omit.
- page_total: 8

- address_lines: ["Hviedzoslavova 1124/31", "974 01 Banská Bystrica", "Slovakia"] — original: "Hviedzoslavova 1124/31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia". Split into lines: ["Hviedzoslavova 1124/31, 974 01 Banská Bystrica, Slovakia"] or split. I'll split: ["Hviedzoslavova 1124/31", "974 01 Banská Bystrica", "Slovakia"].

Wait the source says "(at Ø ≤ 30°C)" — that's "at θ ≤ 30°C" probably (theta water temperature). Yes, Ø is a misOCR of θ. So condition is water temperature ≤ 30 °C.

Also for lower: type_level: maximum_permitted_error_lower_flowrates: {min:-5, max:5} %.

The characteristics value objects: each needs value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers per rule 2? The shape shows those keys; rule 3 says leave unit_id null unless certain. Some unit_ids are certain-ish, e.g., u:degree_Celsius? The instructions: "Leave unit_id: null unless you are certain of the unitsdb ID." I'll leave null everywhere to be safe.

For string values (classes), do I need unit_symbol and unit_id? The strict shape applies to "every characteristic value". I'll include unit_symbol: null and omit unit_id/footnote_markers where empty... Actually to be consistent, include "unit_symbol": null and "footnote_markers": [] for all. Hmm, might be verbose but fine. Let me include unit_symbol always (null if none), and footnote_markers only when present. I'll include unit_id: null too. Let's keep consistent full shape: value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers.
